_law: WS06 (audit 2026-11-05 item 6): research answers may only RELEASE after a server-enforced action/citation/claim check — in TypeScript (lib/chat/answer-release.ts, wired by lib/chat/web-tool-loop.ts) and in Rust (crates/ruke-server/src/chat/answer_release.rs, wired by chat/web_loop.rs). This matrix is the ONE truth for the repair semantics: both sides read these exact bytes (vitest reads this file; Rust include_str!'s it). No brand/site rules — inputs are generic. MHR-D (brief 2026-11-05): the mhrD section byte-locks the NON-DESTRUCTIVE diagnosis (same detectors as the audit, reporting only) and the exact harness-feedback message injected into the existing tool loop when an answer is held back — the MODEL then decides the next action (retrieve / re-attach citations / state the gap). MHR-F (WS26, 2026-11-06) evolved the release law and retired that half-state: the `cases` below now pin CITATION-INTEGRITY-ONLY release — a marker that resolves to NO minted source is stripped, sentence semantics are NEVER rewritten, and a minted citation is never removed; semantic support is REPORTED to the model through the mhrD diagnosis/feedback. The mhrF section pins the separation.

mhrD._law: MHR-D (brief 2026-11-05): the SAME detectors run NON-DESTRUCTIVELY first — diagnoseResearchAnswer reports the actual harness state (fabricated [S#] markers, sentences whose volatile/mis-cited claims resolve to NO minted source, research wording on a zero-retrieval turn) without rewriting a byte. When the loop holds such an answer back, the harness injects ONE feedback message into the EXISTING tool loop (this matrix byte-locks it) and the MODEL decides the next action: retrieve more, re-attach citations, or state the gap. One feedback per turn; the model then continues with tools still armed — no second research engine. Feedback triggers whenever any diagnosis field is non-empty.

mhrF._law: MHR-F (WS26, 2026-11-06): CITATION INTEGRITY and SEMANTIC SUPPORT are separate concerns with separate owners. Integrity is the HARNESS's: the [S#] grammar is minted by the server, so a marker resolving to NO minted source is a broken reference — the release path strips the marker bytes (whitespace/punctuation residue cleanup only) and NEVER otherwise touches the sentence's words. A marker that DOES resolve is never removed, moved or altered, even when an adjacent marker in the same sentence is fabricated. Semantic SUPPORT is the MODEL's job: the mhrD diagnosis reports unsupported claims and fabricated markers to the model ONCE (byte-locked harness feedback; the model then retrieves / re-attaches / states the gap). The release path no longer qualifies any sentence with '(unverified)' — the volatile-word detectors live in the diagnosis ONLY. The SERVER_CHECK_LINE is a server attestation computed from the turn's own action ledger (a fact about the harness, not a content rewrite) and stays in force. releaseCases pin the release law; separationCases pin that the SAME input still diagnoses (semantics REPORTED to the model) while releasing integrity-only. Known limitation (shared with MHR-D, documented not hidden): the diagnosis cannot see the human's own turn, so a re-stated user constraint is still REPORTED (one self-healing feedback round) even though it now releases byte-intact.
